body.estimand_functional: \[R_2(G_n)\asymp r_{\log}(n,d_n),\qquad r_{\log}(n,d)=\frac{d^2}{n\log(d+1)},\] with the upper edge attained by the total graph-dependent procedure \(\mathsf{Compile}(G_n)\) and the lower edge taken over every outcome-independent assignment law and every measurable, possibly randomized estimator.

sampling_model.design: The simple labeled \(d_n\)-regular graph \(G_n\) is drawn uniformly and fully revealed before the experimenter chooses one graph-measurable assignment law. The total compiler first tests \(d_n^2+1<n\): failure returns the all-treated law immediately, while success permits it to evaluate the candidate law that draws \(k_{n,d_n}\) uniform seeds with replacement and treats the union of their closed neighborhoods.
sampling_model.units: Conditional on the revealed graph, the population \(V_n\) and the complete potential-outcome schedule \(y\) are fixed. The schedule may depend on \(G_n\).
sampling_model.treatment: One binary assignment \(Z\) is drawn. The observed data are exactly \(G_n,Z,Y\), where \(Y_i=y_i(Z)\); estimator randomization \(U\) is independent and included in risk.
sampling_model.overlap: No Bernoulli overlap condition is imposed. On the seed branch, the inverse probability \(\pi_i^{(0)}\) is formed only when \(d_n^2+1<n\), which makes it positive; every other finite case uses the all-treated fallback.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: There are no nuisance regressions or prior outcomes. Intermediate-exposure outcomes are unrestricted and ignored.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Corollary 5.4 gives \(d/n\lesssim R_2(G)\lesssim d^2/n\) with high probability for uniform random \(d\)-regular graphs when \(d=o(\sqrt n)\).
Theorem 4.1 bounds the modified Horvitz--Thompson variance by a universal constant times \(\lambda(\mathcal H)/n\) times the endpoint empirical second moments.
Theorem 4.8 gives a polynomial exposure-variance guarantee for randomized one-hop-max clustering under restricted growth and bounded outcomes.
Theorem 1.1 gives \(O(\sqrt d)\) control of the nontrivial adjacency spectrum for uniform simple regular graphs through \(d=O(n^{2/3})\).
The main graph-matrix theorems bound norms of fixed polynomial shapes under the uniform random-regular law by switching trace moments.
Corollary 1 proves a spectral-gap result for Boolean graph powering in a sparse Erd\H{o}s--R\'{e}nyi regime under a small-radius condition.
The paper proves that the independence number is asymptotic to \(2n\log d/d\) for its growing-degree uniform random-regular regime.
The paper gives necessary and sufficient conditions for unbiasedness and consistency of its design-based Riesz estimator class.

body.tldr: This field-tier paper closes the exact all-procedure minimax-rate question of Kandiros--Harshaw--S\'{a}vje for the full global treatment effect on a revealed uniform simple random regular network under their endpoint empirical second-moment class. The proposed answer is \(d_n^2/[n\log(d_n+1)]\). The balanced all-procedure converse, the neighborhood-seed and Rao--Blackwell construction, and the exhaustive finite compiler are inherited infrastructure from \texttt{exp\_randomregular\_fullgate\_minimax\_frontier\_v1}, not new contributions. A supporting sparse-range Boolean estimate and an exact fourth-trace decomposition isolate the sole genuinely new root-level mathematical obligation: a cancellation-sensitive signed four-root switching estimate for \(n^{2/5}\le d_n=o(\sqrt n)\). Establishing that estimate yields the missing upper edge and converts the inherited logarithmic bracket into a matched frontier on the unchanged published class and unrestricted procedure space.

project_justification.gap: Kandiros--Harshaw--S\'{a}vje, Corollary 5.4, studies the identical \(q=2\) GATE minimax game and leaves \(d_n/n\lesssim R_2(G_n)\lesssim d_n^2/n\). The archived \texttt{exp\_randomregular\_fullgate\_minimax\_frontier\_v1} derivation supplies, as inherited infrastructure, the sharper all-procedure lower edge \(d_n^2/[n\log(d_n+1)]\), the seed-design upper certificate of order \(d_n^2/n\), and a total exhaustive compiler, but it leaves a logarithmic gap.
project_justification.niche: A field-tier closure is available if typical random-regular radius-two geometry supports the inherited two-arm seed procedure at the lower-bound scale while retaining Boolean collision cancellations before operator bounds are taken.
project_justification.fill: The paper audits and reuses the inherited balanced converse, seed construction, and finite compiler; proves the separate sparse-range supporting estimate; and concentrates its sole new root-level obligation in a signed four-root completion-switching bound. That bound, the bookkeeping trace identity, and the inherited ingredients yield the matching upper and lower edges uniformly over every admissible degree sequence.

body.related_work: KandirosHarshawSavje2026Minimax, Introduction, Proposition 2.2, Corollary 5.4, Appendix E.4, and the Conclusion, is the sole theorem-level comparator: it supplies the exact decision-theoretic framing and the published \(d_n/n\)-to-\(d_n^2/n\) bracket, and the matched-frontier theorem strictly tightens that corollary on the same class. The balanced all-procedure converse, seed and Rao--Blackwell spine, exhaustive finite compiler, and finite enumeration checks from \texttt{exp\_randomregular\_fullgate\_minimax\_frontier\_v1} are inherited internal infrastructure rather than contributions of this paper. KandirosEtAl2024ConflictGraph, Algorithm 1 and Theorem 4.1, informs the exposure-weight and covariance-operator architecture but is not a claimed tightening target. UganderYin2023RGCR, Section 3 and Theorem 4.8, informs randomized graph decompositions and integrated exposure probabilities under a different outcome class and fixed-estimator guarantee. CookGoldsteinJohnson2018, Theorem 1.1, supplies published adjacency spectral control on the uniform simple regular law; it does not control Boolean radius-two collisions. Xu2025SwitchingGraphMatrices, LIPIcs 339, Article 11, Section 2.2, Theorems 14--15, and the trace-moment construction, informs the switching handle for fixed polynomial graph matrices. AbbeBoixRalliSandon2020, Corollary 1 and Section 2.2, informs the distinction between Boolean graph powering and walk counts under sparse small-radius conditions. CooperEtAl2002RandomRegular supplies degree-growth random-regular context through ordinary independence-number asymptotics; it is not the source of a causal assumption or of the inherited balanced two-arm converse. HarshawSavjeWang2022Riesz informs the design-based estimator language without supplying a complete class for this unrestricted game. Public January 2026 Li--Li slides are non-archival and disclose only a one-arm upper construction under stronger outcome bounds, so they are context rather than a theorem-level comparator. KarrerEtAl2021Scale is the concrete consumer: its deployed cluster-randomized GATE framework receives a random-regular precision benchmark, not a claim that its platform graph is random regular.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The load-bearing dense statement is the signed inequality \(\mathbb E[(B_{12}-p_{n,d})(B_{23}-p_{n,d})(B_{34}-p_{n,d})(B_{41}-p_{n,d})]\le C d^4/n^3\). It is the sole genuinely new root-level obligation. Bounding its five uncentered joint probabilities separately loses the independent-witness and shared-witness cancellations. The exhaustive finite enumeration checks and compiler machinery are inherited from \texttt{exp\_randomregular\_fullgate\_minimax\_frontier\_v1}; their \(n=8,d=3\) verification has no asymptotic force and is not a new contribution. A failure of this sufficient fourth-moment route would not refute the minimax target; the direct Schur-covariance certificate or a different attaining design would remain logically available.
body.honest_scope: Every numbered result is to be proved or independently audited. The signed dense four-root estimate is the sole genuinely new root-level mathematical obligation and is not a maintained assumption. The sparse Boolean estimate is a separate supporting input. The balanced all-procedure converse, neighborhood-seed and Rao--Blackwell spine, exhaustive finite compiler, and finite enumeration checks are inherited infrastructure from \texttt{exp\_randomregular\_fullgate\_minimax\_frontier\_v1}, not claimed contributions. The field-tier result closes the Kandiros--Harshaw--S\'{a}vje rate bracket on one assignment, fixed finite-population potential outcomes, arbitrary neighborhood interference, endpoint empirical second moments, and the unrestricted outcome-blind procedure space. It makes no computational-efficiency claim beyond the inherited finite exact algorithm. As a sanity reduction outside the diverging-degree theorem, at \(d=0\) the same decision problem is the classical no-interference ATE problem and has minimax MSE of order \(n^{-1}\).
